To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
consumers use a retailer’s price reputation as a top-down cue to infer the price of the product being considered.

(a) consumers’ perceptions of prices are affected by retailer price image, and this effect is not accounted for by reference price theories, (b) consumers’ estimates of the prices of products sold at retailers with high price images are lower than those sold at retailers with low price images, and (c) consumers’ choices of products sold at high-price-image retailers are more price-sensitive than those sold at low-price-image retailers.
consumers use price image as a heuristic to infer a retailer’s current offer price, and this heuristic is more accurate and more useful than the prevailing reference price theories.
